Counterexample: `fs-cauchy-riemann-at-a-point-implies-complex-differentiability` has
   \[
   u_x(0)=v_y(0)=1,\qquad u_y(0)=v_x(0)=0,
   \]
   so the definition gives \(\partial_{\bar z}f(0)=0\), but its difference quotient equals \(1\) on real increments and \(-1\) on \(t(1+i)\). Thus it is not complex differentiable at \(0\). See the [theorem title and qualified Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann.md:4), [page summary](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/library/complex-analysis/complex-differentiability-and-cauchy-riemann.md:38), [Wirtinger definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-wirtinger-derivatives.md:26), and [counterexample](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/fs-cauchy-riemann-at-a-point-implies-complex-differentiability.md:42).

   **Severity: fatal** — false title and false founding-page prose.

2. **`ex-square-map-sends-a-grid-to-orthogonal-parabolas` — title and Example.**

   The title says the Cartesian grid becomes “two orthogonal families of parabolas away from its critical point,” and the Example calls all vertical and horizontal grid-line images parabolic arcs. But for \(c=0\),
   \[
   x=0\longmapsto (u,v)=(-y^2,0),
   \]
   whose image is the nonpositive real ray, not a parabola. Removing \(z=0\) leaves a straight open ray, so the “away from its critical point” qualifier does not cure the claim. The proof itself admits this in step 2.1, with the analogous positive ray in step 2.2. The cited treatment also restricts the orthogonal-parabola assertion to nonzero line constants. [Howell–Mathews §9.1](https://complexanalysis.org/web/sec_conformal-mappings.html)

   See the [title, Example, and contradictory case computation](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-square-map-sends-a-grid-to-orthogonal-parabolas.md:4).

   **Severity: fatal** — the title and displayed Example assert more than the verification establishes.

3. **`fs-real-differentiability-implies-complex-differentiability` — `[L1]` and proof step 1.1.**

   `[L1]` attributes “conjugation corresponds to \((x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)\)” to `thm-complex-numbers-are-the-real-coordinate-plane`. That dependency’s Statement only gives the bijection
   \[
   \Phi(a+bi)=(a,b)
   \]
   and the coordinate formulas for addition and multiplication; it says nothing about conjugation. The relevant conjugation definition is in another published item, absent from this item’s dependencies. Compare [the inaccurate `[L1]`](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/fs-real-differentiability-implies-complex-differentiability.md:30) with the [cited dependency’s Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-complex-numbers-are-the-real-coordinate-plane.md:26).

   **Severity: fatal** — inaccurate dependency citation, although the counterexample itself is mathematically valid.

4. **`thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself` — `[L5]` and proof step 4.1.**

   `[L5]` says `thm-continuous-partials-and-cauchy-riemann-imply-holomorphic` gives complex differentiability “with derivative \(u_x+iv_x\).” The cited theorem’s Statement concludes only complex differentiability, and then holomorphy pointwise; it does not state the derivative formula. Step 4.1 relies on that enlarged conclusion to identify \(\exp'(z)\).

   Compare [the inflated `[L5]` and its use](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself.md:51) with the [cited theorem’s exact Statement](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-continuous-partials-and-cauchy-riemann-imply-holomorphic.md:27).

   **Severity: fatal** — inaccurate citation with an added conclusion.
